scope: Proposition 3.7 (Tuning with fixed rounded charges) of the manuscript “Continuum Coulomb hardness with binary nuclear charges” (preprints/Continuum-Coulomb-hardness-with-binary-nuclear-charges-September-24-2026/Continuum-Coulomb-hardness-with-binary-nuclear-charges-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 275 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 290f40f845dc3e0d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: At any fixed rational centers satisfying the hypotheses of this section, and with the integer charges in (3.2) already fixed, one can compute rational ρ1, . . . , ρm ∈ [1, 4] such that |λi + 1/2| ≤ e−1.01D (1 ≤ i ≤ m). (3.38) The algorithm is deterministic and polynomial in D, m and the input bit lengths. Every parameter it samples or outputs has O(D) fractional bits.
